description: OPTIONAL classical dosha-cancellation (parihara) rules. These modify or waive a koota's dosha under stated conditions. Every rule is DISABLED by default. No exception applies unless its `enabled` flag is set true here AND its `citation` slot is verified during domain review.

policy.statement: No dosha cancellation is applied by the engine unless the specific rule below is enabled:true. Enabling any rule is a domain-review + founder decision, not an engineering default.
policy.trace_requirement: Whenever an enabled exception fires, its `id` MUST be recorded in the compatibility report's calculation trace. Silent cancellation is prohibited. The trace must show the raw koota score, the exception id applied, and the resulting score.

exceptions.description: Nadi dosha is considered cancelled when both partners share the same Moon rashi but have different janma nakshatras (one classical parihara).
Nadi dosha is considered cancelled when both share the same janma nakshatra but fall in different padas (quarters).
Nadi dosha is considered mitigated when the lords of the two Moon rashis are mutual friends (school-dependent).
Bhakoot dosha is considered cancelled when both Moon rashis share the same ruling planet (e.g. 6/8 between Aries & Scorpio both ruled by Mars, or 2/12 between signs of one lord).
Bhakoot dosha is considered mitigated when the two rashi lords are mutual friends (school-dependent).
Deva/Rakshasa or Manushya/Rakshasa Gana affliction is considered mitigated when the rashi lords are friends or the moons are favorably placed (school-dependent).

Mangal (Manglik / Kuja) dosha is NOT part of the 36-point Ashtakoota total. It is a separate matching consideration. If DilChat later evaluates it, the neutralization/matching rules live here and are independently enabled and cited. Included as a disabled placeholder so it is never silently folded into the Guna score.

notes: Cancellation rules vary substantially by school and by author; they are intentionally shipped disabled so the base pack produces the raw classical 36-point score.
Mangal dosha is deliberately kept OUT of the Ashtakoota 36-point sum (DEC-019 score-family separation); it may only ever be a separate flag.
